title.narrative: Providing multi-sectoral assistance to provide lifesaving activities while strengthening coping mechanisms and resilience among IDP sites in Rakhine

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed consortium project is a continuation of long-standing consortium between CDN-ZOA and PIN. It builds on the implementation of 4 former MHF projects, MM-21/DDA-3415/SA1/WASH-SNFI-P-N-FS/INGO/18662, 16842, 20745, 23085 and the currently implemented 24105 in addition to MHF reserve allocations provided to both PIN and CDN in the aftermath of Cyclone Mocha. The consortium comprises of CDN-ZOA, PIN, CERA, MUCN, PfP and Shwe Buthi (2 INGOs and 4 CSOs) covering sites in 4 townships: Sittwe, Kyuaktaw, Maruk U and Buthidaung.lt/pgtltpgtThe proposed project is designed based on the assessment and data collected through HNO/HRP 2023, Mocha Rapid Needs Assessments, OCHA Sitrep Report No.4, Humanitarian Update No. 27, and information from partners and local field teams operating within the project target locations. lt/pgtltpgtThe humanitarian situation in Myanmar continues to deteriorate, with premature closure of displacement camps, intensifying conflict and the impact of Cyclone Mocha has only worsened the dire humanitarian situation and plunging whole communities into crisis by damaging and destroying infrastructure and disrupting livelihoods. Cyclone Mocha impacted 1.6 million people, in Rakhine over 824,000 people were affected, which includes an already increased displaced population from AA-MAF fighting in 2022 which saw the total number of displaced people 91,000 (24,483M, 31,991W, 16,661B, 17,995G).lt/pgtltpgtAccess to many areas across the state and additional regulatory requirements have obstructed humanitarian assistance and serves to further compound the severity of the crisis. lt/pgtltpgtThe project has been designed to reach affected communities using low profile approaches through partners and field-based workers and alternative implementation approaches to ensure that support can reach more people, more quickly despite these impediments. Drawing on the partnerships with local CSOs and field workers, and in line with localization policies within CDN-ZOA and PIN this approach will enable the consortium to remain flexible and responsive as demanded by the operating context. The partnership approach used enables a high degree of experience sharing, learning and capacity strengthening. Protection and disability inclusion have been mainstreamed across activities to ensure that those who are most impacted by these crises receive the support they require and to address the increasing protection issues which arise from negative coping mechanisms. The interventions have been co-designed between all partners to ensure that activities are needs driven, address gaps in support, avoid duplication and align with the priorities of relevant clusters in Rakhine.lt/pgtltpgtThe project will respond to the most urgent Shelter/NFI/CCIM, WASH, Nutrition, Food Security and Protection needs of 4,950ltbgt lt/bgthouseholds across 57 sites in the 4 townships which represents more than 30% of the total amount of IDPs stemming from the MAF-AA conflict. Using an integrated multi-sectoral approach, this intervention will contribute to the reduction of a wide range of immediate and life-threatening risks. It will also enhance localization efforts in identified sectors and locations, in particular CCCM in IDP sites for increased sustainability for these populations. The project will target the wider IDP population with a focus on people with specific vulnerabilities.lt/pgtltpgtDuring this project PIN, with collaboration and expertise from UNHCR, will initiate work to pilot nationalization of CCCM for site in Mrauk U currently managed by PIN.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
